ALEX WAN.name: Alex Wan
ALEX WAN.background: Atlanta native whose family moved from South Carolina when he was three; DeKalb County Schools graduate; has lived in Morningside for more than 30 years. B.S. in industrial engineering from Georgia Tech and an MBA (finance) from Wharton (University of Pennsylvania). Former small-business owner of an engineering firm, development director at Jerusalem House, and Emory University development/community-affairs executive (described in 2025 as an Emory vice president); former executive director of Horizons Atlanta. Atlanta City Council District 6 member 2010-2018 and again since Jan. 3, 2022 (succeeding Jennifer Ide); re-elected unopposed Nov. 4, 2025. Lost the 2017 City Council president runoff to Felicia Moore (45.5%) and the June 9, 2020 Georgia House District 57 Democratic primary to Stacey Evans (Wan 32.4%, Evans 56.8%). First openly gay and first Asian American member of the Atlanta City Council (Bay Area Reporter). Board roles have included the Piedmont Park Conservancy, Atlanta Regional Commission (former), Leadership Atlanta and Leadership DeKalb (past chair), and the Mayor's LGBT Advisory Board (former).
ALEX WAN.ideology: Democrat. Atlanta Progressive News, a progressive outlet, ranked him the 'least progressive member' of the Atlanta City Council in October 2011 on its own 18-vote scorecard (score 25/100), citing votes such as supporting the City Hall East sale, waiving affordable-housing requirements for that redevelopment and pension reform. In 2025 he stressed fiscal responsibility, which he called 'unsexy' but necessary (Bay Area Reporter).
ALEX WAN.record: Three terms representing District 6 on the Atlanta City Council (2010-2018, 2022-present; current term ends Jan. 2030). Votes cited by Atlanta Progressive News in 2011 included supporting the sale of City Hall East, waiving affordable-housing requirements for its redevelopment, supporting Mayor Kasim Reed's veto of a sewage-treatment contract, supporting pension reform for existing employees and voting against extending bar hours to 4 a.m.

JOHN BARROW.name: John Barrow
JOHN BARROW.background: Democrat; born Oct. 31, 1955, in Athens, Georgia, son of Judge James Barrow. B.A. in political science and history, University of Georgia (1976); J.D., Harvard Law School (1979); attorney in private practice. Athens-Clarke County Commissioner 1990-2004. U.S. Representative for Georgia's 12th District, Jan. 2005 to Jan. 2015; lost re-election in 2014 to Republican Rick Allen. Democratic nominee for Secretary of State in 2018 (lost Dec. 4 runoff to Brad Raffensperger, 51.9%-48.1%). Ran for the Georgia Supreme Court in 2020 (election canceled after Justice Blackwell's resignation; his lawsuit lost 6-2) and in 2024 (lost to Justice Andrew Pinson, 55.0%-45.0%). Baptist.
JOHN BARROW.ideology: Wikipedia describes him as a Blue Dog Democrat and member of the New Democrat Coalition who chaired the Blue Dog Coalition for policy (2011-2013) and administration (2013-2015), and says GovTrack classified him as a centrist Democrat.
JOHN BARROW.record: Ten years in Congress as one of the most conservative House Democrats from the Deep South; after 2010 the only white Democratic congressman from the Deep South (Wikipedia). Voted for the 2009 stimulus and auto bailout, against the 2009 cap-and-trade bill and the ACA, for the 2006 Federal Marriage Amendment and for Don't Ask, Don't Tell repeal (2010); declined his salary during the 2013 shutdown. Won the 2018 Democratic primary for Secretary of State outright with 51.5%, finished with 48.7% in November and lost the runoff. In 2024 the Judicial Qualifications Commission alleged that his abortion statements violated judicial-campaign ethics rules; a federal judge dismissed his suit challenging the complaint the week before the election (NBC News). Kemp's PAC spent $500,000 for Pinson.
JOHN BARROW.notes: Same person across all four listed races (2018 SOS primary/general/runoff and 2024 nonpartisan Supreme Court race).
